hero.lede: We develop the Triangular Spatial Relationship (TSR) method: an alignment-free way of describing a biomolecular 3D structure as a set of integer keys, so that structures can be compared, clustered and searched without superimposition. BioTSR, our software, computes those keys.

researchVision.heading: Toward Deciphering Molecular Recognition
researchVision.question: Is there a general molecular recognition code that governs how biomolecules recognize one another and how those interactions reshape molecular structure?
researchVision.body: Comparing TSR keys across structures can identify conserved, altered, and interaction-associated spatial patterns. Our long-term goal is to combine these interpretable structural descriptors with machine learning, AI-generated structures, and simulation-derived ensembles to connect structural prediction with mechanistic understanding.

software.heading: BioTSR
software.intro: BioTSR is the group's software for computing TSR keys: one Python package and one command line for the methods described on this site.
highlights: Four calculation families: protein Cα, atomic protein, ligands, carbohydrates and nucleotides, and cross TSR for the interface between two molecules.
Whole datasets from one CSV manifest, processed in parallel as part of the standard installation.
Common keys from the command line; similarity, clustering and a clustered heat map from Python.

research.heading: Methods & research
research.intro: The core representation has been extended to amino acids, drugs, ligands, nucleotides and the interfaces between molecules, and the keys it produces are analysed and modelled in several ways. Each method has its own page explaining the science and the paper behind it.
research.methodsCard: Amino-acid grouping, mirror images, size filtering, secondary structure, amino acids, drugs, nucleotides and nucleotide–protein interfaces.
research.analysisCard: Finding the keys structures share, clustering structures by key similarity, and models trained on key frequencies.
research.earlierCard: The programs the methods were first published with, and separate tools written for particular papers.

group.heading: The research group
group.intro: TSR is developed jointly by the Department of Chemistry and the School of Computing and Informatics at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, bringing together faculty, doctoral researchers and undergraduate students from chemistry, biology and computer science.

funding.heading: Funding & Support
funding.primarySupport: TSR research has been supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS), and the Louisiana Board of Regents Support Fund. contact.heading: Working with us
contact.body: We welcome questions about the method, about using BioTSR on your own structures, and about research collaboration. Problems with the software are best reported as issues on the relevant repository.
